tasks.short: Write up our pay and benefits research as the yearly reward report, salary handbook and works council memo.

today.trigger: Once a year, after the salary benchmark, the CAO costing or the yearly pay review closes. Also when the HR Director or the works council (OR) asks for a written explanation.
steps: Pull the figures from the Power BI HR dashboard and Excel exports from AFAS Profit (pay by grade, site, gender, flex share)
Gather notes from benchmark files, CAO texts and earlier reports on SharePoint
Write the report or manual section in Word, with charts copied from Excel
Rewrite one version for the management team and another in plain Dutch for the OR or the intranet
Send it for review to the HR Director and Finance, then publish it on SharePoint or Teams
drudgery: Rebuilding the same charts and tables each year
Rewriting one text for three audiences
Checking that every number in the text matches the source file
today.time_sinks: Most of the 16 hours goes to the first draft and to the second and third versions for other readers. Checking numbers against Power BI after each round of edits also takes time.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the report and the audience versions from the approved figures table and last year's report, so the specialist spends their time checking and correcting the text. The 16 hours drop to about 9, including a full check of every number.
lenses.autonomous: When the nightly AFAS extract for the pay review period is marked final, a script fills the figure tables and a model drafts the text. Nothing is published until the specialist and the HR Director approve it.
lenses.ambitious: A new service for the works council and employees: a short pay-transparency note in plain Dutch every quarter that explains bands and pay differences per site, ahead of the EU 2023/970 duty that starts with the 2027 pay report. Demand would grow if it got cheaper, because the OR and employees can ask for pay information at any time.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding charts and rewriting the same paragraph three times. The specialist wants more time to work out what the numbers mean and to talk it through with the OR and the managers.
lenses.options: Drafting two or three ways to explain the same pay gap (by grade, by site, by job family) helps the specialist choose the one that is accurate and that the OR will accept. This changes what goes in the report, not only how fast it is written.
lenses.altitude: The specialist's week moves from writing to deciding what the organisation says about pay and on what evidence. They become the editor of Noordhaven's pay story to the OR and staff, which needs more expertise in pay transparency law.
reach: Some of the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's yearly report text: needs better Power BI and DAX skills to check the figures themselves
Pay commentary for the FP&A Analyst's personnel cost section of the budget: needs to learn how the budget model is built

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to publish and how to explain a pay difference fairly, knowing what the OR will read into a sentence, and taking responsibility for every number that goes out under Noordhaven's name.
tasks.pattern_why: It happens once a year, every report has a different shape and audience, and the specialist leads the argument. A model speeds up drafting and rewording but does not decide the content.

in_practice.trigger: The pay review or benchmark is closed and the specialist marks the figures table as final in SharePoint.
steps: A script exports the approved figure tables from the Power BI and AFAS extract to Excel
The model drafts the report sections from the tables, last year's report and the CAO notes, and marks every number with its source cell
The model writes a management version and a plain Dutch version for the OR or intranet
The specialist checks the numbers and rewrites the explanations
The HR Director approves and the report is published on SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist checks every figure and explanation. The HR Director approves before anything goes to the OR, management or staff.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or an approved LLM in the M365 tenant
data_needed: Aggregated pay data by grade, site, gender and contract type (no individual names)
Last year's report and house style
CAO pay scales and benchmark findings
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint report folder with the draft versions, the source figures table and the approval note.

evidence.claim: General-purpose LLMs draft and rewrite reports from tables and earlier texts for different readers.
Noordhaven must report yearly on pay differences, first over 2027 pay by 7 June 2028, and a gap of 5% or more that remains unexplained leads to a joint evaluation with the works council.
AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as preparation for pay transparency reporting.

risks: A wrong or made-up number in a published pay report damages trust with the OR and may count as an incorrect pay transparency disclosure
Small groups in tables (one site, one grade) can identify individuals under the AVG/GDPR
Text that sounds smooth can hide a weak explanation for a pay gap
research_questions: How many hours did last year's reward report and OR memo actually take, and which parts of the work took them?
Does the OR accept a model-drafted text if the figures and the final wording are checked by a person?
Can Microsoft 365 Copilot in Noordhaven's tenant read the Power BI extracts without copying pay data outside the tenant?
What minimum group size does Noordhaven need in published tables to avoid identifying individuals?

role.altitude: From building pay files and grading jobs one at a time to owning Noordhaven's job architecture and the evidence for every pay difference, including the yearly pay transparency report to the works council.
reach: Pay gap figures and dashboard checks from the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Personnel cost assumptions in the FP&A Analyst's budget
First-line answers to pay and benefits questions now handled by HR Administrators
role.ceiling_note: Grading CAO jobs stays inside the CAO system, and the OR must consent to any change in the pay or grading system (WOR 27). Pay decisions cannot be made by a model alone (GDPR Art. 22), and grade or pay recommendations may be high-risk under the AI Act from December 2027. Negotiation, complaints and OR consultation stay with people.
skills_to_grow: EU pay transparency directive and the Dutch implementation
Job evaluation on the four factors (skills, responsibilities, effort, working conditions)
Power BI and basic SQL to check figures without help
Checking AI drafts against source data and keeping audit logs
Explaining pay to the OR and staff in plain Dutch
role.ambitious_version: Run a standing pay transparency service: every role has a band and a documented grade, every pay difference has a written reason, and employees and the OR get clear answers well within two months, with flex workers from the three agencies included.
